text:
A small point of mass $m$ is placed at a distance $2R$ from the centre ' $O$ ' of a big uniform solid sphere of mass M and radius R . The gravitational force on ' m ' due to M is $\mathrm{F}_{1}$. A spherical part of radius $\mathrm{R}/3$ is removed from the big sphere as shown in the figure and the gravitational force on m due to remaining part of $M$ is found to be $F_{2}$. The value of ratio $F_{1}:F_{2}$ is


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The removed sphere of radius $\dfrac{R}{3}$ touches the surface of the big sphere on the side of $m$, so its centre is at $R-\dfrac{R}{3}=\dfrac{2R}{3}$ from O and at $2R-\dfrac{2R}{3}=\dfrac{4R}{3}$ from $m$.


[IMG]

For uniform density, mass scales as the cube of the radius, so the removed mass is

$M^{'}=M\left (\frac{R/3}{R}\right )^{3}=\frac{M}{27}$

Force due to the whole sphere:

$F_{1}=\frac{GMm}{(2R)^{2}}=\frac{GMm}{4R^{2}}$

The remaining part exerts the force of the whole sphere minus that of the removed sphere, both directed along the same line towards O:

$F_{2}=\frac{GMm}{4R^{2}}-\frac{G⎛⎝\dfrac{M}{27}⎞⎠m}{⎛⎝\dfrac{4R}{3}⎞⎠^{2}}=\frac{GMm}{4R^{2}}-\frac{GMm}{48R^{2}}=\frac{GMm}{4R^{2}}\left (1-\frac{1}{12}\right )=\frac{11}{12}\cdot \frac{GMm}{4R^{2}}$

$\frac{F_{1}}{F_{2}}=\frac{12}{11}\Rightarrow F_{1}:F_{2}=12:11$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: If $B$ is magnetic field and $μ_{0}$ is permeability of free space, then the dimensions of $(B/μ_{0})$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the dimensions of $\left (\frac{B}{μ_{0}}\right )$, we start with the formula for the magnetic field $B$ inside a solenoid:

$B=μ_{0}nI$

where $n=\frac{N}{L}$ is the number of turns per unit length, $I$ is the current, and $μ_{0}$ is the permeability of free space.

Rearranging the formula gives:

$\frac{B}{μ_{0}}=nI=\frac{N}{L}I$

From the above, the dimensions of $\left (\frac{B}{μ_{0}}\right )$ are:

$\left [\frac{B}{μ_{0}}\right ]=\left [L^{-1}A\right ]$

Thus, the dimensional formula of $\left (\frac{B}{μ_{0}}\right )$ corresponds to $L^{-1}\text{A}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text:
A uniform circular disc of radius ' $\mathrm{R}$ ' and mass ' $\mathrm{M}$ ' is rotating about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through its centre. A small circular part of radius $R/2$ is removed from the original disc as shown in the figure. Find the moment of inertia of the remaining part of the original disc about the axis as given above.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Mass of removed disc, $m=\frac{M}{πR^{2}}\times π\left (\frac{R}{2}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow m=\frac{M}{4}$

$I=I_{1}-I_{2}$

where, I${}_{1}$ = MOI of whole disc about perpendicular axis through O

I${}_{2}$ = MOI of removed disc about $⊥$ axis through O

$\Rightarrow I=\frac{MR^{2}}{2}-\left [\frac{\frac{M}{4}\left (\frac{R}{2}\right )^{2}}{2}+\frac{M}{4}\left (\frac{R}{2}\right )^{2}\right ]$ (using parallel axis theorem)

$\Rightarrow I=\frac{MR^{2}}{2}-\left (\frac{MR^{2}}{32}+\frac{MR^{2}}{16}\right )$

$\Rightarrow I=MR^{2}\left (\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{32}-\frac{1}{16}\right )=\frac{13}{32}MR^{2}$

$\Rightarrow I=\frac{13}{32}MR^{2}$

text: Two spherical bodies of same materials having radii 0.2 m and 0.8 m are placed in same atmosphere. The temperature of the smaller body is 800 K and temperature of the bigger body is 400 K . If the energy radiated from the smaller body is E, the energy radiated from the bigger body is (assume, effect of the surrounding temperature to be negligible),
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the energy radiated by two spherical bodies, both made of the same material but with different radii and temperatures, we can use the Stefan-Boltzmann law. This law states that the energy radiated by a black body per unit time is proportional to the product of the surface area $A$ and the fourth power of its temperature $T$.

The formula for power $P$ is given by:

$P=σeAT^{4}$

Where:

$σ$ is the Stefan-Boltzmann constant

$e$ is the emissivity of the material

$A$ is the surface area of the sphere

$T$ is the temperature in Kelvin

Expressing this relationship as a proportionality:

$P\propto AT^{4}$

For a sphere, the surface area $A$ is:

$A=4πR^{2}$

Hence, the power radiated is proportional to:

$P\propto R^{2}T^{4}$

For two bodies with radii $R_{1}$ and $R_{2}$, and temperatures $T_{1}$ and $T_{2}$, the ratio of their powers is:

$\frac{P_{1}}{P_{2}}=\left (\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}\right )^{2}\left (\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}\right )^{4}$

Given:

$R_{1}=0.2\text{m}$, $T_{1}=800\text{K}$

$R_{2}=0.8\text{m}$, $T_{2}=400\text{K}$

Substituting into the formula:

$\frac{E}{E^{'}}=\left (\frac{0.2}{0.8}\right )^{2}\left (\frac{800}{400}\right )^{4}$

Calculating each part:

$\left (\frac{0.2}{0.8}\right )^{2}=\left (\frac{1}{4}\right )^{2}=\frac{1}{16}$

$\left (\frac{800}{400}\right )^{4}=2^{4}=16$

Combining these calculations:

$\frac{E}{E^{'}}=\frac{1}{16}\times 16=1$

This implies that the energy radiated by the bigger body $E^{'}$ equals the energy radiated by the smaller body $E$. Thus, $E^{'}=E$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text:
In the diagram given below, there are three lenses formed. Considering negligible thickness of each of them as compared to $|R_{1}|$ and $|R_{2}|$, i.e., the radii of curvature for upper and lower surfaces of the glass lens, the power of the combination is


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For thin layers in contact, applying $\dfrac{μ_{2}}{v}-\dfrac{μ_{1}}{u}=\dfrac{μ_{2}-μ_{1}}{R}$ at each surface in turn and adding (air on both outer sides) gives $\dfrac{1}{v}-\dfrac{1}{u}=\sum \dfrac{μ_{\text{after}}-μ_{\text{before}}}{R}$, so the power of the combination is the sum of the powers of the refracting surfaces.

The flat top surface of the water and the flat bottom have $R=\infty$ and contribute nothing.

Taking the downward direction of the light as positive, both curved surfaces of the glass are concave upward, so their centres of curvature lie above them: $R=-|R_{1}|$ for the upper surface and $R=-|R_{2}|$ for the lower surface.

Upper surface, water $\left (\dfrac{4}{3}\right )$ to glass $\left (\dfrac{3}{2}\right )$:

$P_{1}=\dfrac{\frac{3}{2}-\frac{4}{3}}{-|R_{1}|}=-\dfrac{1}{6|R_{1}|}$

Lower surface, glass to water:

$P_{2}=\dfrac{\frac{4}{3}-\frac{3}{2}}{-|R_{2}|}=+\dfrac{1}{6|R_{2}|}$

Power of the combination:

$P=P_{1}+P_{2}=-\dfrac{1}{6}\left (\dfrac{1}{|R_{1}|}-\dfrac{1}{|R_{2}|}\right )$

Taking the light upward reverses both the order of the media and the signs of the radii, so the power is the same.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
A bob of mass $m$ is suspended at a point $O$ by a light string of length $l$ and left to perform vertical motion (circular) as shown in figure. Initially, by applying horizontal velocity $v_{0}$ at the point ' A ', the string becomes slack when, the bob reaches at the point ' $D$ '. The ratio of the kinetic energy of the bob at the points B and C is $_________$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


As the string becomes slack when the bob reaches at the point D so tension is zero at this point. And the bob just completes the circle.

We know, to complete a vertical loop of radius R, the minimum velocity required at the bottom of loop is $\sqrt{5gR}$.

So, $V_{0}=\sqrt{5gl}=V_{A}$ (as R = $l$)

So, using energy conservation,

$\frac{1}{2}mv_{A}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}mv_{B}^{2}+mgh$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}m(5gl)=\frac{1}{2}mv_{B}^{2}+mg\left (\frac{l}{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow KE_{B}=\frac{mgl}{2}(5-1)=2mgl$

For point C,

$\frac{1}{2}mv_{A}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}mv_{c}^{2}+mg\left (l+\frac{l}{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \frac{5}{2}mgl=KE_{C}+\frac{3mgl}{2}$

$KE_{C}=\frac{mgl}{2}(5-3)=mgl$

So, $\frac{KE_{B}}{KE_{C}}=\frac{2mgl}{mgl}=2$

text: The work functions of cesium (Cs) and lithium (Li) metals are 1.9 eV and 2.5 eV , respectively. If we incident a light of wavelength 550 nm on these two metal surfaces, then photo-electric effect is possible for the case of
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For light of wavelength $550\text{nm}$, the photon energy is

$E=\frac{hc}{λ}=\frac{1240\text{eV nm}}{550\text{nm}}\approx 2.25\text{eV}$

Photoelectric emission occurs only when the photon energy exceeds the work function of the metal.

For Cs, $𝜙=1.9\text{eV}<2.25\text{eV}$, so photoelectrons are emitted.

For Li, $𝜙=2.5\text{eV}>2.25\text{eV}$, so no photoelectrons are emitted.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: A closed organ and an open organ tube are filled by two different gases having same bulk modulus but different densities $ρ_{1}$ and $ρ_{2}$, respectively. The frequency of $9^{\text{th}}$ harmonic of closed tube is identical with $4^{\text{th}}$ harmonic of open tube. If the length of the closed tube is 10 cm and the density ratio of the gases is $ρ_{1}:ρ_{2}=1:16$, then the length of the open tube is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, for closed pipe,

$f_{n}=\frac{nv}{4l},n=1,3,5,7$

for open pipe, $f_{n}=\frac{nv}{2L},n=1,2,3,4$

So, 9${}^{th}$ harmonic of closed pipe $=\frac{9v_{1}}{4l_{1}}$

4${}^{th}$ harmonic of open pipe $=\frac{4v_{2}}{2l_{2}}=\frac{2v_{2}}{l_{2}}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{9v_{1}}{4l_{1}}=\frac{2v_{2}}{l_{2}}\Rightarrow \frac{l_{2}}{l_{1}}=\frac{8}{9}\frac{v_{2}}{v_{1}}$

We know, $v=\sqrt{\frac{β}{ρ}}$

So, $\frac{v_{2}}{v_{1}}=\sqrt{\frac{ρ_{1}}{ρ_{2}}}$ (for same $β$)

hence, $\frac{l_{2}}{l_{1}}=\frac{8}{9}\sqrt{\frac{ρ_{1}}{ρ_{2}}}=\frac{8}{9}\sqrt{\frac{1}{16}}=\frac{8}{9}\times \frac{1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow l_{2}=\frac{2}{9}\times l_{1}\Rightarrow l_{2}=\frac{2}{9}\times 10=\frac{20}{9}cm$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement-I : The equivalent emf of two nonideal batteries connected in parallel is smaller than either of the two emfs.

Statement-II : The equivalent internal resistance of two nonideal batteries connected in parallel is smaller than the internal resistance of either of the two batteries.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true
Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For two batteries $(E_{1},r_{1})$ and $(E_{2},r_{2})$ in parallel,

$E_{eq}=\dfrac{E_{1}r_{2}+E_{2}r_{1}}{r_{1}+r_{2}},r_{eq}=\dfrac{r_{1}r_{2}}{r_{1}+r_{2}}$

$E_{eq}$ is a weighted average of the two emfs. Taking $E_{1}\leq E_{2}$,

$E_{eq}-E_{1}=\dfrac{r_{1}(E_{2}-E_{1})}{r_{1}+r_{2}}\geq 0,E_{2}-E_{eq}=\dfrac{r_{2}(E_{2}-E_{1})}{r_{1}+r_{2}}\geq 0$

So $E_{1}\leq E_{eq}\leq E_{2}$: the equivalent emf lies between the two emfs and is never smaller than both (for equal emfs it equals $E$). Statement-I is false.

$r_{eq}=r_{1}\cdot \dfrac{r_{2}}{r_{1}+r_{2}}<r_{1}$ and likewise $r_{eq}=r_{2}\cdot \dfrac{r_{1}}{r_{1}+r_{2}}<r_{2}$, so the equivalent internal resistance is smaller than either. Statement-II is true.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text: An electron in the ground state of the hydrogen atom has the orbital radius of $5.3\times 10^{-11}\mathrm{m}$ while that for the electron in third excited state is $8.48\times 10^{-10}\mathrm{m}$. The ratio of the de Broglie wavelengths of electron in the excited state to that in the ground state is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, $λ=\frac{h}{mv}$

and $mvr=\frac{nh}{2π}$

$\Rightarrow mv=\frac{nh}{2πr}$

So, $λ=\frac{h}{nh}2πr=2π\frac{r}{n}$

$\Rightarrow λ\propto \frac{r}{n}$

We can write, $\frac{λ_{g}}{λ_{e}}=\left (\frac{r_{g}}{r_{e}}\right )\left (\frac{n_{e}}{n_{g}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \frac{λ_{g}}{λ_{e}}=\left (\frac{5.3\times 10^{-11}}{84.8\times 10^{-11}}\right )\left (\frac{4}{1}\right )=\frac{1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{λ_{e}}{λ_{g}}=4$

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I: In a vernier callipers, one vernier scale division is always smaller than one main scale division.

Statement II : The vernier constant is given by one main scale division multiplied by the number of vernier scale divisions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In a vernier callipers, $N$ vernier scale divisions coincide with $(N-1)$ main scale divisions, so

$1\text{VSD}=\dfrac{N-1}{N}\text{MSD}<1\text{MSD},$

and Statement I is true.

The vernier constant is

$\text{VC}=1\text{MSD}-1\text{VSD}=\dfrac{1\text{MSD}}{N},$

that is, one main scale division divided by, not multiplied by, the number of vernier scale divisions, so Statement II is false.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

So, $v_{x}$ = constant

Now, for y-direction, using Ist equation of motion,

$=1.6\times 10^{7}$ m/s

$\Rightarrow v_{y}=16\times 10^{6}$ m/s.

text: Which of the following resistivity ( $ρ$ ) $\mathrm{v}/\mathrm{s}$ temperature ( T ) curves is most suitable to be used in wire bound standard resistors?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A standard resistor must keep its resistance almost unchanged when the temperature changes, so it is wound from an alloy such as manganin, constantan or nichrome, whose resistivity is fairly large and depends only weakly on temperature.

For such an alloy $ρ=ρ_{0}[1+α(T-T_{0})]$ with a very small $α$, so the $ρ$–$T$ graph is a nearly flat straight line with a large intercept, as in curve (D).

Curve (A) rises steeply, and curves (B) and (C) fall with temperature, so a resistor with any of them would drift in value with temperature.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: Given is a thin convex lens of glass (refractive index $μ$ ) and each side having radius of curvature $R$. One side is polished for complete reflection. At what distance from the lens, an object be placed on the optic axis so that the image gets formed on the object itself?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


We know, for a combination of a lens and a mirror,

$P_{comb}=2P_{l}+P_{m}$ ...... (1)

Also using lens maker formula,

$\frac{1}{f_{l}}=(μ-1)\left (\frac{1}{R}-\frac{1}{-R}\right )=(μ-1)\frac{2}{R}$

So using eq. (i),

$-\frac{1}{f_{comb}}=2\left (\frac{1}{f_{l}}\right )-\frac{1}{f_{m}}$

$\Rightarrow -\frac{1}{f_{comb}}=\frac{4(μ-1)}{R}-\frac{1}{\left (-\frac{R}{2}\right )}$

$\Rightarrow -\frac{1}{f_{comb}}=\frac{4(μ-1)}{R}+\frac{2}{R}$

$\Rightarrow -\frac{1}{f_{comb}}=\frac{2}{R}(2μ-2+1)=\frac{2}{R}(2μ-1)$

$\Rightarrow f_{comb}=\frac{-R}{2(2μ-1)}$

$\Rightarrow R_{comb}=2f_{comb}=\frac{-2R}{-2(2μ-1)}=\frac{-R}{2μ-1}$

Hence, distance $=\frac{R}{2μ-1}$

text: A parallel-plate capacitor of capacitance $40μ\mathrm{F}$ is connected to a 100 V power supply. Now the intermediate space between the plates is filled with a dielectric material of dielectric constant $\mathrm{K}=2$. Due to the introduction of dielectric material, the extra charge and the change in the electrostatic energy in the capacitor, respectively, are
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $K=2,C=40μF,V=100V$

$\Delta q=(KC)V-CV$ (As $q=CV$)

$=(K-1)CV$

$=(2-1)\times 40\times 10^{-6}\times 100=4\times 10^{-3}C$

$\Delta q=4mC$

$\Delta u=\frac{1}{2}C^{'}V^{2}-\frac{1}{2}CV^{2}$

$=\frac{1}{2}V^{2}(C^{'}-C)=\frac{1}{2}V^{2}(KC-C)$

$=\frac{1}{2}V^{2}C(K-1)=\frac{1}{2}\times 10^{4}\times 40\times 10^{-6}(2-1)$

$=\Delta u=2\times 10^{-1}=0.2J$

$\Rightarrow \Delta u=0.2J$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion-(A) : If Young's double slit experiment is performed in an optically denser medium than air, then the consecutive fringes come closer.

Reason-(R) : The speed of light reduces in an optically denser medium than air while its frequency does not change.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, in YDSE,

$β$ (fringe width) $=\frac{λD}{d}$

In denser medium, $λ↓\Rightarrow β↓$

$\Rightarrow$ fringes come closer.

Also, $μ=\frac{c}{v}\Rightarrow v=\frac{c}{μ}$

$\Rightarrow μ↑\Rightarrow v↓\Rightarrow$ speed of light reduces.

frequency remains same,

$\Rightarrow μ=\frac{λ_{vac.}f}{λ_{med.}f}\Rightarrow λ_{med}=\frac{λ_{vac.}}{μ}$ (as $v=λf$)

Hence, option C is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text: The driver sitting inside a parked car is watching vehicles approaching from behind with the help of his side view mirror, which is a convex mirror with radius of curvature $\mathrm{R}=2\mathrm{m}$. Another car approaches him from behind with a uniform speed of $90\mathrm{km}/\mathrm{hr}$. When the car is at a distance of 24 m from him, the magnitude of the acceleration of the image of the car in the side view mirror is ' $a$ '. The value of $100a$ is $__________$ $\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $R=2\text{m}$, so the convex mirror has $f=+\dfrac{R}{2}=+1\text{m}$; the car moves uniformly at $90\text{km h}^{-1}=25\text{m s}^{-1}$.


[IMG]

With the pole as origin and the car on the incident side, at the instant considered $u=-24\text{m}$, $\dfrac{du}{dt}=+25\text{m s}^{-1}$ (the car approaches the mirror) and $\dfrac{d^{2}u}{dt^{2}}=0$.

From the mirror formula $\dfrac{1}{v}+\dfrac{1}{u}=\dfrac{1}{f}$, with distances in metres:

$v=\frac{uf}{u-f}=\frac{u}{u-1}=1+\frac{1}{u-1}$

Differentiating with respect to time:

$\frac{dv}{dt}=-\frac{1}{(u-1)^{2}}\frac{du}{dt},\frac{d^{2}v}{dt^{2}}=\frac{2}{(u-1)^{3}}\left (\frac{du}{dt}\right )^{2}$

At $u=-24\text{m}$, $u-1=-25\text{m}$, so the image velocity is $\dfrac{dv}{dt}=-\dfrac{25}{625}=-\dfrac{1}{25}\text{m s}^{-1}$ and the image acceleration is

$\frac{d^{2}v}{dt^{2}}=\frac{2\times 25^{2}}{(-25)^{3}}=-\frac{2}{25}=-0.08\text{m s}^{-2}$

So $a=0.08\text{m s}^{-2}$ and $100a=8$.

Hence, the answer is 8.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text: Two soap bubbles of radius 2 cm and 4 cm , respectively, are in contact with each other. The radius of curvature of the common surface, in cm , is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the radius of curvature of the common surface between two soap bubbles, we use the formula:

$r=\left |\frac{r_{1}\cdot r_{2}}{r_{1}-r_{2}}\right |$

Given that $r_{1}=2\text{cm}$ and $r_{2}=4\text{cm}$, we substitute these values into the formula:

$r=\left |\frac{2\cdot 4}{2-4}\right |=\left |\frac{8}{-2}\right |=4\text{cm}$

Thus, the radius of curvature of the common surface is $4~\text{cm}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

(Given : $\mathrm{k}_{1}=60\mathrm{Js}^{-1}\mathrm{m}^{-1}\mathrm{K}^{-1},\mathrm{k}_{2}=120\mathrm{Js}^{-1}\mathrm{m}^{-1}\mathrm{K}^{-1},\mathrm{k}_{3}=135\mathrm{Js}^{-1}\mathrm{m}^{-1}\mathrm{K}^{-1}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$R_{1}=\frac{2L}{K_{1}A}$

(As $l_{1}=l_{2}=l_{3}=l$

$A_{1}=A_{2}=A/2$

$A_{3}=A$)

$R_{2}=\frac{2L}{K_{2}A}$

$R_{3}=\frac{L}{K_{3}A}$

$I_{1}+I_{2}=I_{3}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{100-θ}{\frac{2L}{K1A}}+\frac{100-θ}{\frac{2L}{K2A}}=\frac{θ-0}{\frac{L}{K3A}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{100-θ}{2}(K_{1}+K_{2})=K_{3}θ$

$\Rightarrow 50(K_{1}+K_{2})=θ\left [K_{3}+\frac{K_{1}+K_{2}}{2}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow 50(60+120)=θ\left [135+\frac{60+120}{2}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow 50\times 180=θ(135+90)$

$\Rightarrow θ=\frac{50\times 180}{225}$

$\Rightarrow θ=40^{\circ }C$

text:
The position vectors of two 1 kg particles, (A) and (B), are given by

$\vec{\mathrm{r}}_{\mathrm{A}}=\left (α_{1}\mathrm{t}^{2}\hat{i}+α_{2}\mathrm{t}\hat{j}+α_{3}\mathrm{t}\hat{k}\right )\mathrm{m}\text{and}\vec{\mathrm{r}}_{\mathrm{B}}=\left (β_{1}\mathrm{t}\hat{i}+β_{2}\mathrm{t}^{2}\hat{j}+β_{3}\mathrm{t}\hat{k}\right )\mathrm{m}\text{, respectively;}$

$\left (α_{1}=1\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2},α_{2}=3n\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s},α_{3}=2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s},β_{1}=2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s},β_{2}=-1\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2},β_{3}=4p\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}\right )$, where t is time, n and $p$ are constants. At $t=1\mathrm{s},\left |V_{A}\leftarrow \right |=\left |V_{B}\leftarrow \right |$ and velocities $⃗{V}_{A}$ and $⃗{V}_{B}$ of the particles are orthogonal to each other. At $t=1\mathrm{s}$, the magnitude of angular momentum of particle (A) with respect to the position of particle (B) is $\sqrt{\mathrm{L}}\mathrm{kgm}^{2}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. The value of L is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $m_{A}=1kg=m_{B}$

$\vec{r_{A}}=(α_{1}t^{2}\hat{i}+α_{2}t\hat{j}+α_{3}t\widehat{k})m$

$\vec{r_{B}}=(β_{1}t\hat{i}+β_{2}t^{2}\hat{j}+β_{3}t\widehat{k})m$

$(α_{1}=1m/s^{2},α_{2}=3nm/s,α_{3}=2m/s$

$β_{1}=2m/s,β_{2}=-1m/s^{2},β_{3}=4pm/s)$

$V_{A}\leftarrow =\frac{d\vec{r_{A}}}{dt}=2t\hat{i}+3n\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}$

$V_{B}\leftarrow =\frac{d\vec{r_{B}}}{dt}=2\hat{i}-2t\hat{j}+4p\widehat{k}$

$V_{A}\leftarrow .V_{B}\leftarrow =0$ (As $V_{A}\leftarrow ⊥V_{B}\leftarrow$ given)

$\Rightarrow 4t-6nt+8p=0$

At $t=1$, $4-6n+8p=0$

$\Rightarrow 2-3n+4p=0$

$\Rightarrow 3n=2+4p$ ..... (1)

given, $\left |V_{A}\leftarrow \right |=\left |V_{B}\leftarrow \right |$

$\Rightarrow 4+9n^{2}+4=4+4+16p^{2}$

$\Rightarrow (2+4p)^{2}=16p^{2}$ (from (1))

$\Rightarrow 4+16p^{2}+16p=16p^{2}$

$\Rightarrow p=-\frac{1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow 3n=2+4\left (-\frac{1}{4}\right )=1\Rightarrow n=\frac{1}{3}$

Now, $\vec{L}=m_{A}\left (\vec{r}_{A/B}\times \vec{v}_{A}\right )$

at $t=1\sec ,$

$r_{\frac{A}{B}}\leftarrow =(α_{1}-β_{1})\hat{i}+(α_{2}-β_{2})\hat{j}+(α_{3}-β_{3})\widehat{k}$

$\Rightarrow r_{\frac{A}{B}}\leftarrow =(1-2)\hat{i}+(3n+1)\hat{j}+(2-4p)\widehat{k}$

$=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\widehat{k}$

$\vec{L}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \widehat{k} \\ -1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \end{array}\right |$

$=\hat{i}(4-3)-\hat{j}(-2-6)+\widehat{k}(-1-4)$

$\vec{L}=\hat{i}+8\hat{j}-5\widehat{k}$

$\Rightarrow \left |\vec{L}\right |=\sqrt{1^{2}+8^{2}+(-5)^{2}}=\sqrt{1+64+25}$

$\Rightarrow \left |\vec{L}\right |=\sqrt{90}$ kg m${}^{2}$ s${}^{-1}$ = $\sqrt{L}$ (given)

So, L = 90

text:
A particle is projected at an angle of $30^{\circ }$ from horizontal at a speed of $60\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. The height traversed by the particle in the first second is $\mathrm{h}_{0}$ and height traversed in the last second, before it reaches the maximum height, is $h_{1}$. The ratio $h_{0}:h_{1}$ is $__________$.

[Take, $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ ]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Time to reach max. height,

$v_{y}=u_{y}-gt$

$0=30-10t\Rightarrow t=3s$

We know, $S_{n}=u+\frac{a}{2}(2n-1)$

So, $h_{0}=S_{1}=30-\frac{10}{2}(2\times 1-1)=30-5=25$ m

and $h_{1}=S_{3}=30-\frac{10}{2}(2\times 3-1)=30-25=5$

Hence, $\frac{h_{0}}{h_{1}}=\frac{25}{5}=5$
